case: Krosno, European City Facility application 03PL000622X, submitted 17 December 2021
status: Draft. Built by Claude from the extracted text of the files in the manifest; every quote was re-checked against its page by script. Not yet reviewed by a Polish speaker.

submitted.value_en: The Municipality of Krosno (organisation: Krosno Municipal Office). Legal name in Polish: Gmina Miasto Krosno.

in_documents.value_en: Krosno is a city with county rights (a municipality that also performs county tasks), i.e. a single local authority with its own LAU code.
in_documents.quote_pl: Krosno jest miastem na prawach powiatu, zlokalizowanym w południowo - wschodniej części Polski, w województwie podkarpackim

later_documents.value_en: Not checked further; status unchanged.

points.doubt: The form category is inferred, not quoted. A person should confirm Krosno applied alone and not on behalf of the functional area (MOF).

submitted.value_en: Not present in the public submitted files. The official figure nearest to the application date would be 45,165 (GUS, 31 Dec 2020), which only appears in a later document.

in_documents.value_en: Local development plan (2020): 46,291 residents at the end of 2019 (GUS Local Data Bank). Low-emission plan 2019 update: table for the city shows 46,565 (2016), 46,600 (2017), 46,511 (2018), 45,147 (2019), and elsewhere 47,223 (31 Dec 2013).
in_documents.quote_pl: Krosno według danych Banku Danych Lokalnych GUS, zajmowało na koniec 2019 r. obszar 44 km2 (4 350 ha) oraz liczyło 46 291 mieszkańców
in_documents.note: The two source documents disagree for 2019: 46,291 (development plan, p. 7 and p. 21) versus 45,147 (low-emission plan, p. 61, table 'Struktura ludności na terenie Miasta Krosno'; 47,223 for 2013 on p. 39). The development plan figure matches what the later State of the City report gives for 2019, so it is the reliable one. The number Krosno typed in the form is unknown.

points.doubt: The 45,147 for 2019 in the low-emission plan looks like an error or a different population concept ('faktyczne miejsce zamieszkania'); a person should pick the year and source. The chart values in the 2023 report are read from extracted chart labels, so the year-to-value pairing should be eyeballed in the PDF.

submitted.value_en: Krosno Zero emission path
submitted.quote: Krosno Zero emission path

in_documents.value_en: The title was created for the 2021 application; it does not appear in the 2019/2020 documents.
in_documents.note: A 2021 choice; no earlier document can contain it.

later_documents.value_en: State of the City 2023 lists the project 'Opracowanie koncepcji inwestycyjnej dotyczącej transformacji energetycznej Miasta Krosna „Krosno Zero emission path”' funded by EUCF.

submitted.value_en: The tick-box answer is not in the public files. From section 2.4 the grant clearly goes at least to external experts/sub-contractors (feasibility study, legal analysis, technical guidelines); whether in-house staff or other positions were also ticked is unknown.
submitted.quote: For the preparation of the investment concept external experts will be engaged in the fields of: renewable energy, energy and climate efficiency, environmental protection, hydrogen technologies, law and finance.

in_documents.value_en: Nothing about how a EUR 60,000 EUCF grant would be split. The only related statement is in the low-emission plan, which says existing city hall staff are enough to implement that plan without new hires.
in_documents.quote_pl: Obecne zasoby ludzkie Urzędu zapewniają sprawną jego realizację bez konieczności zatrudniania dodatkowych pracowników.
in_documents.note: General context only; the allocation is a budgeting choice made when applying.

later_documents.value_en: Not found.

submitted.value_en: Climate neutrality and energy self-sufficiency by 2040, in two phases (to 2030 and 2030-2040). Note that sections 2.5 and 3.2 of the same application say climate neutrality 'by 2050'.
submitted.quote: Krosno goal is to transform to climate neutrality & energy self-sufficiency by 2040. Process will include two phases: till to 2030 and 2030-2040.

in_documents.value_en: No climate-neutrality or energy self-sufficiency target exists in the pre-2021 documents (zero hits for neutralność klimatyczna, zeroemisyjny, samowystarczalność energetyczna, wodór). The low-emission plan's goal for the city is a CO2 cut of at least 20% by 2020; the local development plan lists 'improve energy efficiency of buildings' and 'increase use of renewable energy' as intervention areas for 2021-2030.
in_documents.quote_pl: osiągnięcia zakładanej redukcji emisji CO2 o minimum 20% do 2020 roku
in_documents.note: Differs from the submitted answer: the documents hold an older, much weaker target (minus 20% CO2 by 2020) and general directions (local development plan p. 186: 'Poprawa efektywności energetycznej budynków', 'Zwiększenie wykorzystania energii ze źródeł odnawialnych'). The 2040 neutrality goal is a 2021 political decision; the application cites an attachment 'Summary_Development_Plan' that is not among the files.

later_documents.value_en: The 2024 ZIT strategy only mentions 'dążenie do neutralności klimatycznej' in general terms (p. 107), with no target year for Krosno.

points.doubt: The application itself is inconsistent (2040 in 2.3, 2050 in 2.5 and 3.2). The answer key should accept either, with 2040 as the stated goal of field 2.3.

submitted.value_en: Not spelled out as a gap list; implied by what the grant funds: Krosno lacks a feasibility study for a decentralised heating network with island hybrid systems and green hydrogen, a legal analysis of how the city can support civic energy and an energy community, and technical standards/guidelines for nZEB buildings.
submitted.quote: The grant will fund: 1. Feasibility study for the construction of a decentralized heating network based on island energy production systems

in_documents.value_en: The local development plan lists the underlying deficits: no climate adaptation plan, 57% of municipal buildings need energy-efficiency work, low energy efficiency of buildings, low use of renewables. It does not say that a feasibility study, legal analysis or building standards are missing.
in_documents.quote_pl: 57% budynków miejskich wymaga działań w zakresie podniesienia efektywności
in_documents.note: Documents give the diagnosis of the problem, not the list of missing preparatory studies. The specific gaps (hydrogen, energy community, nZEB guidelines) are 2021 thinking.

later_documents.value_en: Not checked in detail; the 2024 report shows the Krosno Energy Cluster operating (State of the City 2024, p. 109), i.e. the gap was later filled.

points.who_would_know: The EUCF project team led by the Deputy Mayor; Wydział Rozwoju Miasta i Obsługi Inwestorów (institutional development plan p. 55) and the municipal utility MPGK - Krośnieński Holding Komunalny (heat supplier, low-emission plan p. 81).

submitted.value_en: Three items: (1) feasibility study for a decentralised heating network based on island hybrid systems (heat pumps, PV, storage) and a green-hydrogen solution; (2) legal analysis of the city's technical, organisational and financial support for civic energy plus a concept for an energy community; (3) guidelines for technical standards for public, private and residential energy-efficient (nZEB) buildings.
submitted.quote: 2. Legal analysis in the field of technical, organizational and financial support by the city for the development of civic energy

in_documents.value_en: None of the three studies is mentioned. The low-emission plan only lists generic technologies (PV, solar collectors, heat pumps, biomass) and extension of heating lines; no hydrogen, energy storage, energy community or nZEB guidelines.
in_documents.note: A 2021 decision. Searched: studium wykonalności, wodór, magazyn energii, wspólnota energetyczna, energetyka obywatelska, klaster energii: no relevant hits in the three documents.

later_documents.value_en: State of the City 2023 confirms the concept was prepared under EUCF ('Krosno Zero emission path') but does not list the three studies.

submitted.value_en: The Mayor, Piotr Przytocki: supervises the EUCF project and takes final decisions.
submitted.quote: The Mayor - Piotr Przytocki supervises the EUCF project and makes final decisions in the project.

in_documents.value_en: The Mayor (Prezydent) runs the city hall and most units report directly to him; in the local development plan's implementation structure the Mayor is at the top ('Nadzór wdrażania PRL'). His name is not in the documents.
in_documents.quote_pl: Urzędem Miasta zarządza Prezydent wspomagany przez dwóch Zastępców, Sekretarza oraz Skarbnika. Większość komórek organizacyjnych podlega bezpośrednio Prezydentowi Miasta.
in_documents.note: The role is found and consistent with the submitted answer; the person's name and the fact that he supervises this specific project are not.

later_documents.value_en: Piotr Przytocki signs the State of the City 2023 as Prezydent Miasta Krosna.

submitted.value_en: Deputy Mayor Tomasz Soliński manages the project team.
submitted.quote: The team will be managed by the Deputy Mayor of Krosno - Tomasz Soliński.

in_documents.value_en: The local development plan says project teams are supervised directly by the Second Deputy Mayor, supported by the city development department; no name is given, and the EUCF team did not exist yet.
in_documents.quote_pl: Prace poszczególnych zespołów projektowych będą bezpośrednio nadzorowane przez II Zastępcę Prezydenta wspieranego przez Wydział Rozwoju Miasta i Obsługi Inwestorów.
in_documents.note: Role pattern found (a deputy mayor leads project teams); the name Soliński does not appear in any pre-2021 document, and the appointment is a 2021 act (file 'Project_Team_Krosno').

later_documents.value_en: State of the City 2024 mentions Tomasz Soliński only as a city councillor sworn in during 2024 (resolution of 26.09.2024), not as deputy mayor.

points.who_would_know: Mayor's office / Wydział Organizacyjny, Zarządzania Kadrami i Kontroli (institutional development plan, p. 6), which keeps the Mayor's orders.

later_documents.value_en: Not found.

submitted.value_en: The Mayor takes final decisions; the Deputy Mayor runs the team; the team works to a schedule of activities (transformation roadmap) tracking issues, risks and who is responsible for each task; the chairman of the municipal holding takes part in decision-making; stakeholder representatives take part in the process.
submitted.quote: The project team will work on a schedule of activities - transformation roadmap, issues, risks, and the scope of responsibility of people for the performance of specific tasks.

in_documents.value_en: The 2020 plans describe the city's standard project governance: project teams report bottom-up to the coordinating department, then to the Second Deputy Mayor, the Mayor and the advisory bodies; a risk analysis is kept for each project; rules for task teams are in the Organisational Regulations (order no. 143/19) and the EU-projects procedure (order no. 530/16).
in_documents.quote_pl: Proces przepływu informacji monitoringowych będzie przebiegał zgodnie z logiką bottom up, czyli od poziomu zespołów projektowych, do komórki koordynującej
in_documents.note: Consistent with what was submitted (team -> deputy mayor -> mayor, schedule, risks) but written for the local development plan, not for the EUCF project. The formal orders are listed in the institutional plan p. 61.

later_documents.value_en: Not found.

points.who_would_know: City Secretary / Wydział Organizacyjny, Zarządzania Kadrami i Kontroli (institutional development plan p. 6) and Wydział Rozwoju Miasta i Obsługi Inwestorów (coordinating unit, local development plan p. 263).

submitted.quote: Krosnienski Holding Komunalny - municipal utility company managed by Janusz Fic - Chairman of the Board

in_documents.value_en: The company exists in the documents: the institutional plan lists the city's companies (Miejskie Przedsiębiorstwo Gospodarki Komunalnej, Krośnieński Inkubator Technologiczny, Centrum Dziedzictwa Szkła, Towarzystwo Budownictwa Społecznego, Lotnisko), and the low-emission plan names MPGK - Krośnieński Holding Komunalny Sp. z o.o. as the main heat supplier. The chairman's name is not in any of them.
in_documents.quote_pl: Głównym źródłem zaopatrzenia w ciepło miasta Krosno jest Oddział Energetyki Cieplnej wchodzący w skład Miejskiego Przedsiębiorstwa Gospodarki Komunalnej – Krośnieńskiego Holdingu Komunalnego Sp. z o.o.
in_documents.note: Company found (also institutional plan p. 12, where it is listed only as 'Miejskie Przedsiębiorstwo Gospodarki Komunalnej' without the 'Holding' name); the representative Janusz Fic and his role in the EUCF project are not found (searched 'Fic').

later_documents.value_en: State of the City 2023 and 2024 name 'Miejskie Przedsiębiorstwo Gospodarki Komunalnej – Krośnieński Holding Komunalny Sp. z o.o.' repeatedly; the chairman's name was not found there either.

points.who_would_know: Board of MPGK - Krośnieński Holding Komunalny Sp. z o.o.; in city hall, Wydział Gospodarki Komunalnej (institutional development plan p. 6).
points.doubt: The plan lists the company as 'Miejskie Przedsiębiorstwo Gospodarki Komunalnej' and the application as 'Krośnieński Holding Komunalny'; they are the same company (full name combines both).

submitted.value_en: External experts will be engaged in: renewable energy, energy and climate efficiency, environmental protection, hydrogen technologies, law and finance. Internal staff cover project management, external funding and city finance.
submitted.quote: external experts will be engaged in the fields of: renewable energy, energy and climate efficiency, environmental protection, hydrogen technologies, law and finance.

in_documents.value_en: No statement on external experts for an energy investment concept. The low-emission plan claims internal staff are sufficient and lists the in-house profiles needed; the local development plan uses experts of the Association of Polish Cities in an advisory role.
in_documents.quote_pl: Istotną rolę w procesie odegrają eksperci ze Związku Miast Polskich, którzy będą pełnili rolę konsultacyjno-doradczą.
in_documents.note: Differs from the submitted answer: the low-emission plan (p. 151) says current staff can implement it without extra hires, while the application says external experts are needed in six fields. The fields were chosen in 2021 to match the three studies.

later_documents.value_en: Not found.

submitted.value_en: Residents of single-family houses; residents of multi-family houses and housing communities/cooperatives; entrepreneurs, with a separate subgroup of local 'native' entrepreneurs; utility suppliers (electricity and district heating); public entities.
submitted.quote: residents of single-family houses; residents of multi-family houses, communities/cooperatives, entrepreneurs including a separate subgroup of local, "native" entrepreneurs, utility suppliers (electricity and district heating), public entities.

in_documents.value_en: The local development plan has a stakeholder table (Table 33) with categories: youth, seniors, entrepreneurs/investors, business support institutions, NGOs, education, culture and sport, city authorities/offices, districts, housing market entities (TBS, Krośnieńska Spółdzielnia Mieszkaniowa), social assistance, activists, media. The low-emission plan lists the housing cooperatives and the heat supplier.
in_documents.quote_pl: Tabela 33. Interesariusze bezpośrednio zaangażowani w opracowanie Planu Rozwoju Lokalnego
in_documents.note: Overlaps (entrepreneurs, housing cooperatives, public bodies, residents) but the energy-specific split into single-family vs multi-family residents and utility suppliers is not made in the documents. Housing cooperatives: low-emission plan p. 64; table continues on local development plan p. 223.

later_documents.value_en: Not checked.

submitted.value_en: Only indirectly: the transformation should support the community and bottom-up initiatives, with projects that let people reach self-sufficiency and make gains; engagement will communicate these benefits. No need or expectation is given per group.
submitted.quote: The overall transformation includes support for the community, a bottom-up initiative in the field of energy & climate transformation, including projects that allow to attain self-sufficiency and enable gains.

in_documents.value_en: The local development plan records problems rather than stated needs per group: low ecological awareness of residents, low energy efficiency of buildings, low use of renewables; intervention areas include removing non-ecological heat sources and raising ecological awareness of residents and entrepreneurs.
in_documents.quote_pl: Mieszkańcy nie przywiązują wagi do ekologii
in_documents.note: General context only (also p. 186: 'Likwidacja nieekologicznych źródeł ciepła', 'Poprawa świadomości ekologicznej mieszkańców i przedsiębiorców'). Nothing on what each group expects from an energy investment programme (costs, savings, heat prices).

later_documents.value_en: Not checked.

zit_strategy_date.answer: The document is dated 'KROSNO 2024' on its cover. It was commissioned by contract no. RI.021.5.2023.M of 29 May 2023 and cannot have been adopted before mid-October 2024, because it describes public consultations that ran until 16 October 2024. Every page carries a signed-resolution footer ('Id: ... Podpisany'), so it is an annex to an adopted resolution, but the resolution number and date are not in the extracted text. It did not exist in December 2021.

consistency_checks: Totals reproduce: row savings sum to 164.51 GWh and row renewables to 76.1 GWh; Annex E rows sum to EUR 160,644,000.
Savings vs renewables rule is met: 164.51 > 76.1; renewables are 31.6% of total impact.

Annex E lists seven targeted sectors and those seven have non-zero investment; Sustainable urban mobility is EUR 0 and has no Annex D rows, yet the Annex E comment says green hydrogen will fuel public transport buses.
District heating (EUR 5,040,000) and Smart grids (EUR 13,340,000) carry investment but zero energy savings and zero renewable generation in Annex D.

Innovative energy infrastructure is 53.5% of investment (EUR 86,000,000) but delivers no savings, only 44.5 GWh of the 76.1 GWh renewable generation; 92% of savings come from Residential and Public buildings, which get 19.3% of investment (EUR 30,944,000).

CO2 total 'savings' 72,910.29 t is the sum of row values and is larger than before minus after (53,823.59 t) because it adds avoided emissions from renewables; it omits the PV farms (21 GWh, would be about 15,099 t at 719) and heat storage (4.5 GWh), which have blank CO2 cells.
Emission factors are mixed: 'Heat/cold' and coal both 341; hybrid heating that replaces coal and the hydrogen CHP are valued at 202 (natural gas).
Possible double counting of renewables: about 7 GWh of PV electricity is used for hydrogen and the hydrogen CHP output (3.2 GWh) is counted again; heat storage 4.5 GWh is counted as generation.
One Annex D row (10.9 GWh renewable, 2,201.8 t CO2, factor 202) has no legible component name in the text extraction.
Application text inconsistency: climate neutrality 'by 2040' in field 2.3 but 'by 2050' in fields 3.2 and 2.5; field 3.4 gives only 2030 percentage targets, no GWh, while Annex D runs to 2040.

Annex D baselines conflict with the 2019 plan: residential district heat 170 GWh vs 39.6 GWh bought by households (plan p. 84); street lighting 2.9 GWh for 3,500 lamps vs 3.39 GWh for over 6,000 luminaires (plan p. 107); lighting saving 2.11 GWh vs 0.525 GWh for the same 3,500-point scope (plan p. 144).
Evaluator feedback (score 20.50/25; A1 investment 4.0, A2 energy 4.0, B1 4.3, B2 4.5, B3 4.0) raised no inconsistency; only asked for more detail on tasks of the actors.
